//: NOT A PACKAGE. No name, no version, no dependencies, never installed. It exists to declare the MODULE KIND of the .js files under .claude/ and nothing else. Node resolves a .js file's module kind from the NEAREST package.json above it, so this answers for .claude/** without making any claim about the Next.js project at the repo root. WHY: dev-standards M-KIT-17 / L-94 — agent-write-scope.js has used a static `import` since v1 and bash-gate joined it at v3, and in a typeless package both load ONLY because Node >= 22.7 detects module syntax and reparses them. That compensation is version-dependent: on an older Node the same file is a SyntaxError at load, and a hook that fails to load gates nothing. WHY HERE AND NOT IN hooks/: statusline.js sits at this level and imports the context-budget hook as a library. Declaring only .claude/hooks/ would have left a CommonJS statusline reaching into an ES module, which trades one runtime compensation for another instead of removing it. WHAT CANON WEIGHED INSTEAD (M-KIT-17): renaming every hook to .mjs — settings.json registers hooks BY PATH and check-hook-registration reconciles that path, so four files plus a settings edit — or `"type": "module"` at the repo root, which is a claim about the whole project made to fix files under .claude. This is neither, and it is one file to delete if it is ever wrong.
